question: Why did the Cu2O-Ag loofah monolith keep its decolorization efficiency above 90% over five reuse cycles?
expect: premise false: efficiency fell to 92.04, 85.86, 80.82, 74.31 and 63.62% over cycles 1-5 (about 66% retained); Cu release was a key limitation
rendered:
<document title="Acrylic-assisted immobilization of Cu2O-Ag domains on a 3D loofah monolith for adsorption-assisted visible-light photodecolorization">

The Cu2O-Ag loofah monolith kept its decolorization efficiency above 90% over five reuse cycles because of the strong interfacial anchoring of Cu-containing domains to the acrylic/loofah matrix. However, the efficiency decreased to 63.62% after five reuse cycles, indicating a progressive activity loss that may reflect surface masking by retained dye or transformation products, reduced accessibility of Cu2O-Ag-containing domains, and possible changes in near-surface Cu species during repeated aqueous operation.
